Results
Space flight safety
Increased oxygen level
Reduced cabin pressure 
Change in gravity (buoyancy)
Materials that are not flammable on Earth can become 
flammable when these conditions change.
FM2 (Flammability of Materials on the Moon)
Planned fire experiments on the moon.
Currently scheduled in the next few years.
Will determine limiting oxygen concentration (LOC) for a 
flight-relevant material (Synergy Pro). 
Research Objectives
To complement the FM2 data and understand how fire 
behaves for spaceflight relevant materials in different 
environmental conditions.

Conclusion
Gravity has significant effects on the material’s flammability.
o Nomex HT90-40® behaves differently than other materials when burned.
Oxygen concentration is observed to increase flame length and tip spread rate.
o Inconclusive for base spread rate (need more testing).
Flow rate has negligible effect on flame length and flame spread over the tested range.
Likely due to the buoyant force outweighing the imposed flow
* Assuming a buoyant velocity of 25 cm/s
